plates.prompt:
One photorealistic film still for a Sri Lankan television drama, a tall portrait 9:16 frame: the blocking plate of a scene, which shows where each person stands. A single picture, no panels, no gutters.

Reference images, in order: image 1 is the location sheet for Colombo roadside: six named views of the one place, numbered left to right, then top to bottom: view 1 Wide; view 2 Looking left; view 3 Looking right; view 4 Reverse; view 5 Detail 1; view 6 Detail 2; image 2 is the vehicle sheet for Food three-wheeler: six named views of the one vehicle. Take from image 1 the place itself: its buildings, its fixed things and every place that stands in it, their materials and where each one stands. This still is painted from view 1 (Wide)'s camera: paint that view's place, the same things on the same sides. Never copy the sheet's gutters or layout. Take from image 2: ONLY the vehicle itself, exactly as shown: its make and model, body shape and colour, wheels, lights and windows, and its inside: its dashboard, steering and seats. Ignore everything around the vehicle in that picture (its street, ground and light).

People: every person is a smooth, matte, faceless artist's mannequin in one solid colour, with jointed limbs and simple hands: Kasun is the red mannequin; Anudi is the blue mannequin. A small raised ridge on the front of the head, where a nose would be, shows which way the head faces. Each mannequin has the person's real height and build and sits, stands and holds things exactly as a real person would. No faces, no hair, no clothes, no skin: only the mannequin colour. The place, the light and the weather are a real, photorealistic film still.

Props: every prop (phone) and every small thing a person holds or carries is a plain, smooth, matte white clay stand-in of the real object: its real size and outline, and nothing else: no screen, buttons, logo, lettering, pattern or colour. A vehicle is never a clay stand-in: every vehicle is painted real, exactly as its vehicle plate shows it, with its real colours. Each stand-in is held, carried or set down exactly as the real thing would be. The place itself is real: its ground, walls, water, plants, what is built into it, and Colombo roadside, Food three-wheeler, painted as a real photograph, never as clay.

World: Soft early-morning overcast daylight, with fine rain, rain-wet concrete and patched asphalt throughout. Light comes from the road at camera right; the vending shelter creates gentle shade, with restrained roadside greens, earth colours and a softly warm naturalistic grade. Kasun is a smooth, featureless red artist's mannequin of medium height and lean, wiry build; Anudi is a smooth, featureless blue artist's mannequin of average height and slender build. Neither mannequin has clothing or human surface detail. Every portable object is a plain matte white clay stand-in matching its reference outline and scale, including the phone, open folding umbrella, structured handbag and loose tea flask. The older maroon food three-wheeler remains real, with its black vinyl roof, dark-brown trim, raised side hatch and scratched stainless-steel counter with recessed metal trays. Draw no text, symbols, labels or interface details anywhere.

Vehicles: every vehicle is real, never clay, exactly as its vehicle plate shows it: the Food three-wheeler is image 2. Ground marks: Small movements (a turn of the head or body, a lean, a shift of weight, half a step) stay within half a metre of the mark; the feet never travel further. Kasun (the red mannequin) stands on the same concrete landing strip, level with the rear/right end of the three-wheeler's pavement-side serving ledge and 0.6 metres roadward of its front edge. The open side hatch and maroon vehicle body sit behind and left of this position, 1.4 metres to Anudi's left in the road-facing shared views, on the same line parallel to the kerb drain. Anudi (the blue mannequin) also keeps ONE spot for all these shots, where the spots above place them. The gap between them is the same in every panel: a closer camera makes them larger, never closer together. What is behind each of them follows from these spots and the panel's camera.

The camera: ANCHOR SPOT on the road, about two metres out from the drain, camera faces square on toward the pavement and buildings, at standing eye height; a 28mm wide, every mannequin full length with their feet on the ground, and the landmarks their marks name in frame. Hands: the red mannequin: left hand Empty, hanging beside the near-side left hip; right hand Far-side hand gripping the clay phone by its edges, extended toward frame centre. the blue mannequin: left hand Far-side hand gripping the clay umbrella shaft; the clay handbag handles hang over the left forearm; right hand Near-side palm open beneath the clay phone, not yet gripping it. the clay tea flask rests on The rear/right end of the three-wheeler's stainless-steel side serving ledge.

Draw NO text of any kind. The people, place and everyday details are Sri Lankan.
